R_H1.passageTitle: How Lotus Leaves Inspired Self-Cleaning Surfaces

passages.label: A
passages.text: A lotus leaf can remain strikingly clean although it grows above muddy water, and the clean appearance is not produced by polishing. In a study published in 1997, botanists Wilhelm Barthlott and Christoph Neinhuis investigated the surface of sacred lotus and other plants. They asked how leaf structure, water repellency and the weak attachment of dirt worked together. Their research turned an old observation about a plant into a testable explanation of self-cleaning.

passages.label: B
passages.text: A microscope image shows that the leaf is not truly flat. Its surface has a fine relief formed partly by wax crystals. The researchers compared microscopically smooth leaves with rough, water-repellent leaves under controlled conditions. They placed different particles on the plants and then used artificial rain from a sprinkler or fog generator. This comparison separated the effect of roughness from the simple fact that water had touched a leaf.

passages.label: C
passages.text: On a rough, water-repellent leaf, a drop touches less of the surface than it would on a smooth leaf. Dirt also attaches less strongly. As the drop rolls away, its movement collects loose particles. The study found that rolling drops removed the artificial contamination from the water-repellent leaves. Both parts of the mechanism are essential: water must form moving drops, and particles must attach more strongly to the water than to the leaf.

passages.label: D
passages.text: Biomimicry does not require engineers to manufacture a plastic lotus leaf. They can translate the principle by combining a water-repellent material with a carefully structured surface. The University of Bonn reports that this research influenced a range of work in paints, varnishes and other surface technologies. The useful idea is the relationship among structure, water and particles, rather than the colour or exact shape of the plant. Where people handle a personal item every day, it is essential to check whether rubbing wears the coating away.

passages.label: E
passages.text: These tests illustrate what a photograph cannot show. A close-up can preview what a coating looks like. How well will the coating work once it rains? Dirt may spread over it or come away in drops. Designers have to rethink the principle across a range of surfaces and conditions. If it could release harmful material or make a wet floor unsafe, it would need more tests. One good result does not mean its uses are unlimited. A drop that cleans one place can leave dirt behind in another.

passages.label: F
passages.text: The discovery offers a technology that a designer in another industry might use to create a product. A diagram can help the user see why the surface matters. Engineers can make a comparison with a plain material and study the outcome before they make a decision about a new use. A promising result may encourage them to make improvements when a coating has to withstand repeated contact.

R_H2.passageTitle: From Shark Riblets to Aircraft Film

passages.label: A
passages.text: Shark skin offers a lesson in what engineers borrow from nature. Its useful feature is a pattern of tiny ribs, rather than a shark-like appearance. An enlarged image can illustrate the ribs because they are hard to see at normal size. Engineers who want to translate the idea to aircraft must rethink it for air rather than water. The ribs need to follow the local movement of air over the aircraft.

passages.label: B
passages.text: Frictional drag develops where air meets an aircraft's outer surface. Riblets guide the near-surface air in the direction of travel and can reduce part of that resistance under suitable conditions. The pattern does not push an aircraft forward. It changes the movement of air very close to the surface. Because the ribs are microscopic, their size, direction and position matter to the result. A random rough surface would not provide the same controlled geometry. The alignment and dimensions of the ribs are essential to how the design works. Another development in the industry may use a different technology.

passages.label: C
passages.text: Lufthansa Technik and BASF made the AeroSHARK film with very small ribs set out in lines. Unlike a cover for a personal device such as a phone, the aircraft film has to follow both the shape of the surface and the direction of flow. It must fit around curves and leave parts accessible to staff who maintain them.

passages.label: D
passages.text: On 14 October 2022, SWISS began passenger operations with a Boeing 777-300ER carrying about 950 square metres of the film on its fuselage and engine nacelles. Lufthansa Technik said simulations calculated fuel and emission savings of just over one per cent for that aircraft type. The scheduled flights were meant to test the estimate in daily operation. That sequence prevents a forecast from being reported as a measured outcome. These details illustrate the difference between a calculated potential and a result still being validated.

passages.label: E
passages.text: In December 2022, the European Union Aviation Safety Agency granted a supplemental type certificate for the 777-300ER and 777F modifications. The certificate allowed series installation on those two variants without extending approval to an unlimited range of aircraft. A sample can preview the surface of the film, but an apparently similar arrangement could be unsafe if installed where the air flows in a different direction. Adoption can spread to other models only when the relevant application is approved. The developers said that using less fuel would reduce carbon dioxide emissions, helping limit the harmful effects of a greenhouse gas. Savings depend on routes, operating conditions and the area covered.

passages.label: F
passages.text: The result depends on how a company plans to install the product and what its measurements allow it to conclude. A diagram of a test device can show the direction of flow. The outcome may encourage an airline to make an investment or the supplier to make improvements. A team needs to make a decision based on evidence from the aircraft where the film was used.

R_H3.passageTitle: Content Credentials and the History of a File

passages.label: A
passages.text: A deepfake can copy the appearance of a person or the sound of a voice, and it can spread before anyone has checked it. A viewer may preview an image before deciding to share it. One option is to inspect the file for signs of changes. Another is to check for a record of where it came from and what happened to it along the way. This record, often called digital provenance, provides evidence under particular conditions.

passages.label: B
passages.text: In February 2021, Adobe, Arm, the BBC, Intel, Microsoft and Truepic formed the Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity, or C2PA. They began developing an open standard for recording the origin and history of a range of digital media, including pictures, video, audio and documents. Under this standard, a Content Credential is a signed record connected to an asset. It can include statements about creation, editing tools, later changes and the use of artificial intelligence. A record may travel inside the file or be linked from another location. A user can access a record through a compatible app on a device. Developers create tools that allow people to inspect the details. The technology helps them make a comparison, while its outcome still depends on which record a product can read.

passages.label: C
passages.text: The system uses cryptographic hashes and digital signatures. A hash acts like a mathematical fingerprint of data. If protected content or its credential changes, validation can show that the new fingerprint no longer matches. A signature also identifies the organisation or system that signed the record, which supports security checks based on known trust lists. A compatible viewer can then present the recorded history to a user instead of hiding it inside technical metadata. When an editor makes a declared change, a new signed record can preserve the earlier one and add the action.

passages.label: D
passages.text: This technology has important limits. A valid credential does not prove that a claim inside a video is true. Even harmful or unsafe material can still have an accurate record of who published it. Provenance may also be incomplete, and metadata can be removed. The absence of a credential is not proof that a file is false, because adoption is voluntary. C2PA therefore describes optional soft bindings, ways to link a file to its history, such as invisible watermarks or fingerprint lookup, that may help recover a remotely stored credential. Their presence gives evidence about history, not a final judgement about meaning. A record may cover a range of actions taken while a file was edited.

passages.label: E
passages.text: Two examples illustrate the limits of the record. A creator may add a name, but a real name is not essential to the standard. That choice helps protect personal privacy. Someone can also sign a clip with harmful claims or pictures that dehumanise a person. A valid signature helps with file security. Deciding whether it would be unsafe to share the clip still takes judgement. Looking at both the record and the source helps a viewer rethink the simple choice between real and fake.

questions.prompt: What does validation compare if protected material has been changed?
options: Whether the new version is easier to view on screen.
Whether a statement in the file has become factually true.
Whether the new fingerprint still matches the earlier one.

questions.instruction: Choose ONE answer, A–C, for each question.
questions.prompt: How does a digital signature contribute to a check using a known trust list?
options: It gives the artwork a title that every viewer sees.
It identifies the signer so that information can be used in the security check.
It guarantees every claim made in the signed material.

questions.instruction: Choose ONE answer, A–C, for each question.
questions.prompt: How can a declared edit be added while keeping the earlier history?
options: Make another signed record that keeps the previous one and adds the change.
Overwrite the earlier record so only the latest action can be found.
Keep only an unconnected description of the latest picture.

questions.instruction: Choose ONE answer, A–C, for each question.
questions.prompt: Who released it is already known. What still has to be checked before one can trust what it says?
options: Whether its account agrees with what actually happened.
Whether a party has been identified as having released it.
Whether it is a format that can carry a link to its history.

questions.instruction: Choose ONE answer, A–C, for each question.
questions.prompt: Why can a file lack a credential without it following that the file is false?
options: Every missing record was removed after a change was found.
Participation in the system is optional.
A file can be checked only if it comes from a new camera.

questions.instruction: Choose ONE answer, A–C, for each question.
questions.prompt: What can optional soft bindings recover while leaving another question open?
options: A person's name even if it was never entered in any record.
A result proving every statement inside the file accurate.
A history kept elsewhere, leaving the content’s meaning open to judgement.

questions.instruction: Choose ONE answer, A–C, for each question.
questions.prompt: What may a creator leave out without breaking the standard?
options: Every piece of information linking the history and the asset.
An action that the text says the creator must declare every time.

questions.instruction: Choose ONE answer, A–C, for each question.
questions.prompt: How can someone with a reason to stay unnamed still give viewers something worth checking?
options: Omit the name so nobody can ever tell whether anything was signed.
Let the item carry an account of how it was made or edited while leaving out a personal identifier.
Publish a person’s details automatically when the item is signed.

questions.instruction: Choose ONE answer, A–C, for each question.
questions.prompt: What is still required when a signed clip may contain harmful claims?
options: Let the existence of a signature settle whether the claims should be shared.
Treat the details as correct as soon as a source has been identified.
Someone still has to judge the consequences of passing it on.

questions.instruction: Choose ONE answer, A–C, for each question.
questions.prompt: Which conclusion captures the article’s lesson about using Content Credentials?
options: Knowing what happened to an item is useful, while examining its message still takes a separate judgement.
Any digital item without a history record must have been fabricated.
A signature establishes that the file is safe to pass on.
